_doc: Rules for ops_watch.py (the Dispatcher's deterministic measurement arm, V3_ROLES_BUILD_EIGHT_CHAIRS_ONE_TABLE). Keys are glob patterns over point keys (family.name). Only MEASURED points feed the band, run and silent rules; a target names the marks it accepts. A target with alarm true files one rimflow item when the condition is NEW, and re-arms only after it clears. Its optional worse is the stated step ({"factor": 2}: doubled; {"add": 50}: 50 further, in the direction its op calls worse) past which an alarm still crossed is raised again (a note, a Conductor line, a fresh Operations run); a rise in severity does that with no step.

relentless._churn_doc: ops_watch.rl_churn: an item is in churn when it failed an attempt (attempts.jsonl end not in churn_not_fail_ends, which holds the put-downs hold and conductor_hold: a person's hold is no failed attempt, OPS_CHURN_DIAGNOSE_HORRORS_XSDJ_RKYR, and the supervisor's own bookkeeping rows reach_adopted, reach_repaired (a probe passed), reach_waiter_released, reach_held and game_env_route (routed, no builder), OPS_CHURN_DIAGNOSE_RETURNED_WORK_IWIV gen 5; the class is the signature) in the last churn_window_h and has churn_returns returns or one class churn_same_class times; returned tokens are the spend-file runs whose (item, gen) failed, placed by the gen's start row

item_bands._why: INITIAL GUESSES (RUNNING_PAGE_BUILD_ROWS_WEAR_THEIR_BOUNCES, owner 2026-11-05): RUNNING_NOW colours each item row cool/warm/hot by its worst value; shared with ops_watch's per-item churn alarm (CHURN_WATCH_BUILD_NAMES_EVERY_BOUNCER) so both read one set of numbers. Each pair is [warm at or over, hot at or over]. passes = 1 + state.json returns: 2 is one bounce, 3 is two. spent = state.json weighted tokens: warm at the advisory item_spend_limit (3M; closed items read p90 3.4M on 2026-11-04), hot at its first doubling (6M). age_s = time in the current stage: warm at the stage's normal top on the page (STAGE_OLD), hot at about 3x. A row FLASHES only for an identified cycler (a circling.py hit at the item's current gen, or in churn by the churn_* rule above) or a stuck process (running/checking with no unit process, or no beat for stuck_silent_s: a worker is told to beat every 20 minutes). Retune from what the page shows.

health._doc: ops_health.py (PIPELINE_BUDGET_ENFORCE_HEAL_THYSELF): Operations' ONE verdict, health.json beside status.json, read by relentless.py to order its pool. Owner 2026-11-03: 'Yes relentless fixes itself first.'; 'I don't want relentless to own assessing system health. I want it to ask "the system" for its health assessment, and that belongs to the operations component.' An SLI is bad past its line; its budget is spent at allowed_bad_h bad hours in window_h (design idea 5: 'When any SLI is over budget for 24 h, Relentless staffs only pipeline items until it recovers'). Spent: degraded, content paused. system_words/system_prefixes classify an open item as the system's own (no game mod named). Words match the id's SUBJECT only, never its twist; a system_words_lead word counts only as the first word (HOSE_NET_SELFTEST is a mod's test). guard_exempt_kinds: alarm kinds no test can guard, a spent account is weather (alarm_census.recurring).

ranges._doc: OP1 in operating_requirements_2026-11-01.md: the watched metrics' classes as data, read by the collectors and by ops_watch.run, which stamps class, owner, ack_within_min and max_age_min on each reading. A metric fills only the classes it can act on, of idle, sane, distressed, emergency (roles.* alone: under, sane; under rings nothing, RO1 is report-only); every class is one of {"at_least": n}, the class of a reading from n up to the next class's n, or {"in": [text]} with one {"otherwise": true}. owner: who answers for it. ack_within_min: required with distressed or emergency. max_age_min: an older source reads UNMEASURED. idle_if: this metric reads idle while any metric named here does. why: a range change rewrites it. `ops_watch.py lint` and load_rules refuse a metric short of any of these. classes: a limit lives here and nowhere else

relentless.why.why: A stop somebody chose reads idle, never distressed: pause, no budget. Anything else is the belt filling. The day's spend ceiling stops nothing since owner 2026-11-02 (TOKEN_LIMITS_TAME_BARK_NO_BITE: token limits advisory everywhere), so it is no reason here.

relentless.ready.why: With nothing ready a silent belt has no work to be late on: no_live_min and progress_age_min read idle.

relentless.tick_age_s.why: staffing.json and reading.json carry their write time, so the age is one tick plus the 2 min timer pause. A deploy plan inside the tick had grown ticks to 3-8 min with outliers to the unit's 20 min kill; since its mod gap reads --gate (35 s, not 260 s) ticks run 1-3 min (RELENTLESS_TICK_TUNE_FIFTEEN_MINUTE_NAPS), and tick_game_budget_s 240 plus gate_plan_max_s 180 stays inside 8 min. Past 10 the tick is slow or dead: its journal row's phases and slow_steps name the step.

relentless.under_min.why: Distressed line equals relentless_rules.json staffing.alarm_after_min (selftest_relentless_watch holds them equal). Emergency at 2 h, four times the distressed line: the 2026-11-01 jam ran 6 h, so this class would have stood for its last 4.

relentless.breaker_open_min.why: The 2026-11-01 jam ran 6 h behind an open breaker. Emergency at 2 h, four times the distressed line: the 2026-11-01 jam ran 6 h, so this class would have stood for its last 4.

relentless.no_live_min.why: Minutes with nothing live; the 2026-11-01 jam held nothing live for 6 h. Its max_age_min bounds staffing.jsonl, the record it is counted from.

relentless.progress_age_min.why: The longest gap between progress acts outside the jam was 25.4 min (2026-10-31 to 11-01), and a worker's run may last 60.

relentless.blind.why: Any source not seen: nothing can say the belt is sane until it is seen again. Agrees with the relentless.blind target.

disk.scratch_outside_cap.why: OP2: 279 clones once sat outside the pool cap, which counts relentless/clones alone. The reading is rm_scratch_clones in the newest phase of scratch_reap's sanity record. Distressed one past that record's start line of 12 (near twice a quiet machine); the selftest holds the two equal. max_age_min: two hourly reaper starts plus the timer's 5 min jitter and a margin, so one missed run is not an alarm and two are.

disk.scratch_outside_blind.why: The sanity record is missing, torn, stale or holds no reading: nothing can say the clones are inside the cap. Agrees with the disk.scratch_outside_blind target.

queues.artpipe.stalled_min.why: QUEUE_ORPHAN_WEDGE_1: pending jobs with no claim, finish or heartbeat for 20 min. The daemon sat IDLE with 37 pending for 17 h behind an orphaned active/ job and a latched sandbox check.

queues.testq.stalled_min.why: QUEUE_ORPHAN_WEDGE_1: testq pending with nothing running or finishing for 20 min (a paused.json reads 0).

queues.arena_ralph_c.stalled_min.why: QUEUE_STALL_ALARM_FINISH_THE_STRAGGLERS: an armed arena with a pending live-test candidate and no claim, run log or result for 60 min: the runners are gone or wedged on an orphan claim (a claim is taken over only after 6 h).

queues.replay_watch.stalled_min.why: QUEUE_STALL_ALARM_FINISH_THE_STRAGGLERS: a replay arm in flight and no replay_watch tick for 30 min: nobody is watching for its death or hang (the watcher's timer was uninstalled 2026-11-04; a relaunch needs a watcher).

queues.designer.stalled_min.why: DESIGNER_STALL_MONITOR_READY_AND_FORGOTTEN: a concept at status=ready with no Designer run for 60 min. The Designer is run-now only, so nothing launches it (FlowWorks sat at stage 2 ready from 2026-11-04 13:02Z for 12 h+ while 14 FlowWorks build items were concept_refused); measured runs take 2 to 11 min. DESIGNER_ANSWERED_MONITOR_WAITING_ON_NOBODY: a waiting_owner concept whose owner has answered counts from his answer, since only a run's open moves it back to ready.

queues.blind.why: A queue whose directories cannot be listed: nothing can say it is moving.

seats.paused.why: A PAUSE file is a stop somebody chose: seats.idle_with_work_min reads idle, never distressed.

seats.tick_age_s.why: last_ok_tick in state.json. Older than max_age_min the source is frozen and seats.blind says so, so no class above sane is needed. The tick runs every 2 min.

seats.idle_with_work_min.why: DI1's 30 min, the owner's limit for FOUNDRY idle with work ready; the 2026-10-31 run crossed it at 14:44Z, before the idle_full_queue alarm of 14:55Z. Emergency at 2 h, four times that line.

seats.blind.why: The state or journal is missing, frozen or disagreeing: nothing can say the seats are sane. Agrees with the seats.blind target.

roles._doc: RO1, role_use.py: how the ledger shows a role's outputs. Report-only: the metric gates nothing and is no target. marked: the words a role's own output carries. coarse: the design's first reading of a role's items, a file event's why opening with the word; reported beside the marked count, acted_share does not use it. action_events: what counts as somebody acting on an item; a note, raise, lease or reassign moves no work.

steve_incident._doc: item-id prefix of the steward's escalation items (testq/steward.py); steve.incident_unclaimed_min is the age of the oldest one no seat holds; owner_rung marks an OWNER rung (the steward's T+120 item before STEWARD_RUNG_FIX_ASKS_THE_WRONG_GROWNUP; that rung is now a told row for Operations), no seat's to claim, never counted

band._doc: a point outside the baseline mean +/- k sigma. Baseline: the last baseline_days of MEASURED points, minus the last exclude_recent_h; needs min_points. Sigma is floored (max of sigma_floor_rel x |mean| and sigma_floor_abs) so a flat series does not flag on noise.

run._doc: n consecutive same-direction changes (equal neighbours collapse) in the KPI series named here; a drift the band cannot see yet.

silent._doc: a series that was MEASURED within the baseline and has not been MEASURED for its hours: the instrument went blind.

targets.name: OPS_CHURN_DIAGNOSE_ITEM
targets.why: CHURN_WATCH_BUILD_NAMES_EVERY_BOUNCER, owner 2026-11-05: 'Please maintain a very tight awareness for churning items please. This needs to be a constant operations monitor, deterministic: what items are just bouncing around the build pipeline, costing more and more, or stuck in testing a very very long time without progress. It raises alarms for operations to look into the issue.' One fixed OPS_ item per churning item (its name from the item's first word and id), raised for Operations; the reading names the item and its reasons (bouncing, spend rising, stuck). The work: read that item's attempts.jsonl and state.json under the relentless store, find why it does not land (a broken test, unreachable evidence, a wrong contract, a game lane that never runs) and fix or file the cause; never only retry it. A worse reading (one more reason) re-raises; it clears when the item stops churning, lands or retires

alarm._doc: Filing: spawn as RUNNER from the dispatch clone (its testq/ingest.py: rimflow + publish) under QHOME/ingest.lock, the lock the ingest and the Dispatcher take. RM_OPS_ALARM_CLONE / RM_OPS_ALARM_PARENT override.
alarm._for_doc: BENCH is relentless's home pool (relentless_rules.json pool_seats/pool_needs), which its workers drain: the 10-31 re-measure, D2. ops_watch and the dead-man file here only while rimflow incident.receiver_problem(for, needs) says somebody picks it up, else the alarm stays PENDING with 'no receiver' on it; every item filed or reopened is raised, so it comes first in relentless pool_order (T2, ALARMS_REWIRE_OFF_RETIRED_BENCH)
alarm._clear_passes_doc: an open alarm clears (and re-arms) only after 4 clear readings in a row (1 h at 15 min): a reading that wobbles across its line files one item, not one per wobble. UNMEASURED readings neither clear nor reset the count (a flaky instrument must not pin an alarm open forever)

token_talk._doc: No-AI drift measure (owner 2026-10-27: only Operations analyses burn; every role but it and the Conductor is token-blind). Per seat and role: the % of its reports in window_days (ledger notes/closes by that seat, commit messages by path owner, finished role-run result text) holding at least one term. Terms are regex fragments, whole-word, case-insensitive; a bare cap is not a term (log caps, size caps), a token/daily/week/session/usage cap is. Operations is excluded (its OPS_* ledger items and its role runs). Under min_reports reports the point is UNMEASURED, never 0.
token_talk._seats_why: owner 2026-10-31: "Conductor accesses everything." Seat BENCH (the Conductor and its helpers) and the conductor role are not measured.

codex._stale_h_doc: a last reading older than this is an ESTIMATE floor: Codex may be spent from another machine
